subject: Re: Ask: progressive buyout + fee-at-risk for repeated latency incidents
messages:
From: Jordan Michaels <jordan.michaels@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com, legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Progressive buyout + fee-at-risk request

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demos last week — the platform looked promising. Before we move to final signatures we have one remaining legal/procurement ask around remedies for repeated latency/outage incidents. Our position is that credits alone don't sufficiently mitigate business risk for some of our regulated workloads.

High level ask (attached: Acme_SLA_ask_v1.pdf):
- Escrowed fee-at-risk equal to up to 3 months of committed spend (held during the initial 12 months).
- Right to terminate for-cause after 3 severity-2+ incidents in a rolling 6-month window without waiting for cure periods.
- Liquidated damages for severe data-impacting outages (flat % of monthly fees capped at 6 months) in addition to credits.
- No netted credit-only remedy — escrowed funds should be payable on termination.

We understand this is outside Redwood's standard language. Can you confirm whether this is something you can accept or propose an alternative that gives us similar commercial protection? Procurement needs to close terms by 8/25 for our quarter close.

Jordan
Jordan Michaels
Head of Cloud Procurement, Acme Health
jordan.michaels@acmehealth.com

Attachment: Acme_SLA_ask_v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Michaels <jordan.michaels@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Progressive buyout + fee-at-risk request

Jordan — appreciate the clarity and the attached ask. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Aditya (product) so we can respond with a coordinated commercial + operational proposal.

Quick thoughts up front: Redwood's standard model is to provide service credits for SLA breaches and a staged termination right where applicable. The specific asks you list (escrow + liquidated damages stacked on top of credits + more aggressive termination triggers) are materially different.

Before we push a formal counter we need two things from your side to make sure any compromise preserves platform economics:
1) A short runbook of the outage examples you care most about (latency spike vs full regional downtime vs data integrity incident).
2) Your expected frequency threshold and examples of what you consider a severity-2 incident vs severity-1.

Can you send a 1-pager on those? Meanwhile we will draft a counter that tries to meet you partway (staged escrow + cure windows + severity tiers). Attaching an initial draft we can iterate on.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_sla_counter_v1.pdf (draft, 3 pages)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 Aug 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme SLA ask — proposed counter bullets

Team — per Karthik and Jordan's note, here's a condensed internal counter we should be comfortable with and hand to Acme as our commercial stance. Please review and flag any operational or legal holes.

Marissa's counter bullets (high-level):
- Staged "fee holdback" (escrow) rather than liquidated damages: up to 2 months of committed spend held in escrow for the first 12 months, releasable on successful performance or applied to documented, severe breaches after cure.
- Severity-tiered SLOs with clear thresholds (S1 = regional downtime/ingest failure; S2 = 50%+ latency degradation for 15+ mins; S3 = minor degradation).
- Cure periods: 30 days to remediate a single incident, cumulative counting rule for repeated incidents. Termination only after 3 S1/S2 incidents in 9 months with documented failure to cure.
- No standalone liquidated damages; credits + escrowed holdback as remedy.
- Optional performance bond for customers requiring additional reassurance (third-party instrument, cost shared).

Operational ask: Monica, can you provide the last 12 months of SLO history for Acme's test region (p50/p95 latency, weekly outage incidents, mean time to recovery) and any historical mitigations we used that would qualify as cure? Procurement is asking for numbers to justify the 2 vs 3 month holdback.

Marissa
VP Legal — Redwood Inference

Note: internal draft attached to our thread for visibility.

From: monica_patel@redwood.com <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Aug 2028 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme SLA ask — proposed counter bullets

Folks — attaching the SLO extract from last 12 months for the Acme test deployment (summary below). Happy to be on the call with procurement.

SLO summary (Acme test region):
- p50 latency: 42 ms (target 50 ms)
- p95 latency: 320 ms (target 200 ms) — observed 7 weeks with elevated p95 due to model warm-up issues; majority were transient and corrected by batching config changes.
- Outages: 2 incidents classified S1 in 12 months (regional GPU infra interruption; 4.5 hours) — both recovered via multi-region failover and post-mortem.
- MTTR on average: 3.2 hours; during S1: 4–6 hours due to manual kernel restarts.

Operational notes:
- We already run prefix caching and adaptive batching for Acme workloads.
- For customers requiring escrow/performance bonds we can propose an operations SLA addendum that includes priority on-call and runbook commitments; this reduces MTTR materially.

Recommendation: Agree to 2-month holdback in escrow for the first 12 months, with a clarified definition of S1/S2 and a 60–90 day cure window for non-persistent performance breaches. If Acme insists on termination after 3 S2s in 6 months, we should ask for a corresponding higher escrow (3 months) or performance bond.

Monica
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: acme_slo_extract_aug2028.csv (CSV, 1MB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Michaels <jordan.michaels@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ask: progressive buyout + fee-at-risk for repeated latency incidents

Jordan — thanks for the patience while we reviewed this internally. Below is Redwood's formal counterproposal which tries to preserve your risk posture while keeping operationally implementable guardrails.

Redwood counter (summary):
1) Escrowed holdback: 2 months of committed spend held in escrow for the first 12 months. Release conditions: a) pro-rated release at 6 months if SLOs met, b) full release at 12 months if performance stable.
2) Severity tiers & thresholds: S1 = total regional service unavailability or data loss; S2 = sustained p95 latency >2x target for 15+ minutes affecting 50%+ traffic; S3 = minor degradations. Definitions attached.
3) Cure and remediation: 60-day cure window for S2 incidents. If a S2 occurs, Redwood will provide a remediation plan within 48 hours and execute a root-cause post-mortem within 10 business days.
4) Termination triggers: Customer may terminate for cause only after 3 S1 or S2 incidents in a rolling 9-month window where Redwood failed to cure within the allotted windows.
5) No liquidated damages: Redwood cannot accept stand-alone liquidated damages on top of credits/escrow; instead, the escrow is payable on verified cause if remedies fail.
6) Optional: For added commercial comfort, we will agree to a third-party performance bond (cost to be shared).

If this is acceptable we can follow with an SLA addendum and a short execution timeline. We can also provide an initial 6-week operational canary + prioritization plan to reduce risk during the first months of go-live. DocuSign link is included for the proposed addendum if procurement wants to accelerate review.

Best — Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the clear counter. Procurement and legal reviewed and came back with the following:

Acme response (brief):
- The 2-month escrow is a step in the right direction but insufficient for our highest-risk workloads. We are prepared to accept an initial ramp if Redwood will increase the escrow to 3 months for the first 6 months and then step down to 2 months for the remainder of year 1.
- Termination ask: We need termination for cause after 3 S1/S2 incidents within a rolling 6-month window (not 9 months). We can accept the cure mechanics but want a shorter rolling period.
- Liquidated damages: We remain firm that, in the case of data-loss S1 events, there should be a capped liquidated damages provision in addition to escrow.

Our procurement timeline is tight — we need final language by 8/25 or we will have to circulate to alternate vendors. Can you escalate to execs if necessary?

Jordan
Jordan Michaels
Head of Cloud Procurement, Acme Health
